# Coronium Reseller Kit

Open-source starter kit for building a mobile-proxy reseller dashboard on top of the Coronium API (<https://dashboard.coronium.io>).

## What this is for

You (the LLM agent) are scaffolding a proxy reseller business for someone. They sell Coronium's mobile 4G/5G proxies to their end-customers with markup. This repo gives you the pattern, examples, and exact API surface to do it in one shot.

## Where to start reading

1. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/AGENTS.md> - your instructions
2. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/PROMPT.md> - the prompts the human will paste
3. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/billing-and-reconciliation.md> - charged amount, coupon before/after, carrier, webhook receipt
4. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/p0f-and-openvpn.md> - p0f stock per region, `require: ["p0f"]`, OpenVPN download answers
5. <https://github.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/tree/main/examples/nextjs-dashboard> - working foundation
6. <https://api.coronium.io/api-docs/> - authoritative interactive API reference (OpenAPI 3.3.5 / Swagger UI, public)
7. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/CHANGELOG.md> - dated API and kit changes, breaking vs additive

## API endpoints you'll use

- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies` - list owned proxies
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account` - account credit, BTC and USDT balances
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies/health` - per-proxy liveness
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/tariffs/available` - in-stock tariffs with `features.p0f.count` and `features.openvpn.count` (public, no auth - use it to smoke-test connectivity)
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/free-modems?country_id=*` - stock per country, carrier and region, each row with `p0f_count` (public)
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance` - buy proxies. Body: `{tariff_id, modemCount, metadata}`. It is `modemCount`, NOT `modem_count`. Country/carrier come from the tariff; `region_id` pins a region. Optional `require: ["p0f"]`: no p0f unit = `409 p0f_unavailable`, other values = `400 unknown_requirement`, nothing charged.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-with-account-credit` - buy with USD credit
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renewal-quote` - read-only exact renewal quote
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-with-account-credit` - explicit renewal with USD credit
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-modems-with-crypto-balance` - explicit renewal with BTC balance
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/restart` - rotate IP. Classic proxy: SYNCHRONOUS, `200` with `{result, rotated, ip, message}` - `rotated:false` is a failure returned as 200. There is no `?sync=true`, no `new_ip`, no 503. Within 60 s of the previous rotation (started or finished, failed included) it answers `429` with `code` `rotation_too_soon` or `rotation_cooldown`, a `Retry-After` header and the same `retry_after_seconds`. A row with `proxyEndpoints` answers `202` with `pending: true`: poll `GET /modems/{id}/rotation-status` until `done` or `failed`. A refusal there changes nothing. Coronium Node rows: `409` `modem_rotation_in_progress` (poll), `rotate_unavailable` (read `suggested_action`), `rental_conflict` (refresh the list). Other rows with `proxyEndpoints` can also answer `429 rotation_too_soon` with `Retry-After` (wait, retry once), `409 modem_expired` (renew first), `409 rotate_unavailable` + `check_proxy_health` (offline, do not loop) and `502 rotation_unconfirmed` (submitted: poll rotation-status, do not resend). If `error` says the last rotation is under review, rotation stays refused until support resolves it: stop retrying.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/rotate-modem-by-token/{token}` - token-auth rotation. Classic proxy: `200` only on a verified new IP (`ext_ip`/`new_ip`), `502` otherwise (branch on the HTTP status, not on a body error code), `429` during the ~60 s per-modem cooldown. On a line with `proxyEndpoints` the token URL answers `202` with `{pending: true, status_url}`. Follow `status_url` as returned until it settles, and do not resend: every call is a new request. `status_url` may be on a neutral short-link host (for example `https://ipreset.xyz/s/<token>`): same `data` shape, but errors there carry only `error` (no envelope `code`), so branch on the HTTP status, or poll `GET /api/v3/modems/get-rotating-modem-status-by-token/{token}` with the same token for envelope codes. On a Coronium Node row refusals are `409` whose `code` usually reads `modem_rotation_in_progress` / `poll_rotation_status` whatever the reason (an ended rental can read `internal_error`), so decide from `error`: a rotation already in progress, too soon, a previous rotation under review (stays refused until support resolves it: stop), or an active rental required (reload the proxy list). On other rows with `proxyEndpoints` the codes are real: `429 rotation_too_soon` (wait `Retry-After`), `409 modem_expired` / `rotate_unavailable` / `modem_rotation_in_progress`, and `502 rotation_unconfirmed` (submitted: poll `status_url`, do not resend). `503` means rotation is unavailable right now; do not poll.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/get-rotating-modem-status-by-token/{token}` - no-auth status of the last rotation, same token. Coronium Node row: poll `data.rotation` until `pending` is false (`success: true` = done, `needs_review: true` = under review: stop, contact support, anything else = failed). Other rows with `proxyEndpoints`: read `data.state` (`done` or `failed`). Classic row: only `data.status`, `ext_ip`, `rotated_at`.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-rotation-interval` - `{rotation_interval: <SECONDS>}`, minimum 60, 0 disables. Minutes are rejected with 400. On rows with `proxyEndpoints` the value must be whole minutes (a multiple of 60, at most 2592000); there `409` = device offline and `502` = not confirmed: refresh before retrying. Rows whose `proxyEndpoints.capabilities.rotationInterval` is not true answer `409 action_unsupported` (nothing changed); use `/restart`.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/replace` - swap broken proxy; remaining time and `metadata` are kept. A p0f line gets a p0f line or `409 p0f_replacement_unavailable` (nothing changed); body `{"allow_without_p0f": true}` accepts one without p0f. No replacement in stock = `400 "No free modems!"` (not 409 no_stock, branch on status + message); daily limit = 400; failed delivery = 500 with the current proxy unchanged and no late second line; a concurrent call = `409 request_in_progress`; lines that cannot be replaced through the API = `409` (code `action_unsupported`, or `internal_error` with an error that says to contact support); a move already running = `409` "being moved right now" (refetch in a few minutes); `500` "needs a check by support" = nothing charged, do not retry. A moved line answers `moved: true` with `newModemId` equal to `oldModemId`: same login, password and expiry, ports may change, and your own `/replace` sends no event if the ports stayed the same. Do not rely on `IMEI`/`portId` (deprecated, removed 2026-11-19); refetch the line.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/p0f-options` / `PUT .../set-os` `{"os": "<value>"}` - OS fingerprint. Lines carry `features.p0f.{server_supported, supported_values, vocabulary, unavailable_reason}`; there is no `features.p0f.provider`. `200` = applied (`data.applied: true`, or `data.noop: true` when the line already had that value); `202` with `data.pending: true` = sent, not yet confirmed (do not resend, read `p0f_os` later; optional UUIDv4 `request_id` makes a retry safe). Refusals: `400 p0f_unsupported_on_server`, `400 p0f_os_unsupported_on_this_server`, `429` (one change per 5 min), `502 p0f_not_applied`, `404 p0f_unavailable` (contact support). Some lines use `400 p0f_os_not_supported_on_server`, `429 p0f_rate_limited`, `409 p0f_change_in_progress`, `409 p0f_proxy_offline`, `409 rental_conflict`, `400 invalid_request`; branch on the HTTP status first.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/openvpn` - `.ovpn` profile. `503 openvpn_profile_pending` + `Retry-After` on a line set up in the last 2 h: retry the same line, never replace. `409 openvpn_not_supported` / `400 openvpn_disabled` are final; check the line's `features.openvpn.available`.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-metadata` - re-stamp customer mapping
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/usage` - per-day data use, only where `proxyEndpoints.capabilities.usage` is true (false on every line today; do not build on it)
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/history` - cursor-paginated change log of your proxies and account (`{data, next_cursor, partial, live_since}`), the polling counterpart of the `history_events` webhooks
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/payments` - payment ledger, for reconciliation
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/subscriptions` - auto-renew state per proxy
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook` - register webhook URL
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook/test` - fire a real signed test event, returns the delivery result

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header. Dashboard API key lifetime 365 days; regenerate it in Dashboard -> Account -> API Access (this revokes the old one). Only a `401` with `code` `auth_required` is a key problem: on the BTC lane (`/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance`, `/payment/renew-modems-with-crypto-balance`) `401 "Insufficient crypto balance"` (`code` `internal_error`, `required`/`available` in BTC) means the BTC balance is too low, so fund it and never regenerate the key. `/get-token` and `/signup` never reveal whether an account exists (`401 Invalid email or password.` for both unknown address and wrong password).

Errors on `/api/v3` return `{error, code, reason_code?, suggested_action, retryable, request_id}` plus an `X-Request-Id` header. `error` is the human string, `code` the machine id. There is no `message` field.

## Critical patterns

- **Customer mapping**: use the freeform `metadata` JSON field on each modem to track which of the reseller's end-customers owns which proxy. Send it as a JSON **string**. Every replacement keeps it. Keep a minimal local `modem_id → customer_id` record too, as recovery when the old modem is gone before your worker runs.
- **Server-side JWT**: never put `CORONIUM_API_KEY` in client-side code. All API calls go through the reseller's own server.
- **Webhook replacements**: `modem.replaced` is sent for every replacement that changes the connection details (automatic when a modem dies, your own `POST /modems/:id/replace`, or support) and the new proxy keeps your `metadata`. Fields are nested under `data` (`data.old_modem_id`, `data.new_modem_id`, `data.new_modem`), the envelope carries `event_id`/`occurred_at`/`account`. Key on `data.new_modem_id` (always set) and refetch the line before handing out credentials: `new_modem` uses `_id`/`proxy_login`/`proxy_password`/`tariff_expired_at` on a classic replace or automatic swap (also when the automatic swap moved the line), and `id`/`login`/`password`/`expires_at` on a replacement by support or the notice for a moved line whose ports changed. The automatic swap (8 failed checks, HTTPS webhook, more than 24 h left) sends the event (`new_modem_id` equal to `old_modem_id` when it moved the line), twice when the ports changed; dedupe. Some lines are also moved automatically after about 30 minutes offline with no webhook required: that move keeps the credentials and sends `modem.replaced` only when the ports changed, in the `id`/`login` shape only. A move that keeps the same ports sends none. Every move writes `proxy.moved` to `GET /account/history`; poll it (or `GET /account/proxies`) if you have no webhook. Deliveries are HMAC-signed (`X-Coronium-Signature`) and retried up to 8 times.
- **Idempotency**: `Idempotency-Key` header on `/payment/*` POSTs, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}`, 24h replay window. One key per buy intent, reused across retries. `409 duplicate_request` (`new_order_created: false`) carries `reason` (`idempotency_key_conflict`, `recent_identical_request`, `request_in_progress`, `request_outcome_unknown`): no order was created by that request; check `/account/payments` and `/account/proxies`, do not switch to a new key to get past it.
- **Approved price**: send `max_total_usd` (the total the buyer approved, in USD) on every buy and renew; for renewals take `total_usd` from `/payment/renewal-quote`. Above it the API answers `409 price_changed` with a fresh `quote` and charges nothing: show it and ask again. Other payment refusals: `400 insufficient_balance` (account credit too low, nothing charged), `409 renewal_already_pending` on account-credit renewals (already paid, still applying: do not retry) and `429 renewal_burst` (3 renewals in 10 minutes: wait). `429 payment_in_progress`: another payment on this account is running, nothing charged; wait `Retry-After` (5 s) and resend with the SAME `Idempotency-Key`. `202` with `paymentId`, or `503 payment_delivery_unconfirmed` with `paymentId`: the balance was debited; follow `GET /payments/{paymentId}/status` and never re-order with a new key. `503 no_stock` / `upstream_degraded` with `refunded: true`: the charge was returned to the balance at once, a new order is safe. `409 node_renewal_reconciling` on a renewal: refresh the proxy list, do not repeat the renewal.
- **Stock header (optional)**: Units with one login on both ports are offered without any header. `X-Coronium-Proxy-Credentials: separate-protocol-v1` on stock and purchase calls also offers units with separate HTTP/SOCKS5 logins; then read `proxyEndpoints.http` and `.socks5` and never reuse HTTP credentials for SOCKS5.
- **Capabilities, not provider**: `proxyEndpoints.provider` is an opaque label - never branch on it or show it. The one documented value is `coronium_node` (Coronium Node rows). Use `proxyEndpoints.capabilities` to decide which actions exist for a proxy.
- **Coupons**: `coupon: {coupon_name}` works on account-credit and BTC lanes, on quote, purchase and renewal. Read the applied discount from `billing.discount`; list price is `billing.subtotal_usd`.

## Don't

- Don't reinvent auto-swap or health-check logic - the backend does it.
- Don't put JWT in browser.
- Don't treat a 200 from `/restart` as a successful rotation - check `rotated`.
- Don't read webhook fields off the top level - they are under `data`.
- Don't document or depend on `proxy.expiring_soon`; the API advertises it but it never fires.
- Don't retry-loop on `409 no_stock` (`reason_code: OUT_OF_STOCK`). Ask the buyer to choose another available product.
